summary: Remote 1935/1936 Aermotor tower in Idaho's Frank Church Wilderness, unstaffed since 1997 and under long-term stabilization.

facts.status_note: Unstaffed since 1997; undergoing multi-year stabilization by Payette National Forest staff and volunteers.

access.note: Reachable only by an 18-mile foot or horseback trail in designated wilderness; not open for rental or climbing.

events.note: NHLR gives 1935 as the build year for the 72-foot Aermotor tower.
Rocky Mountain-style log cabin ground house added as lookout residence.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Idaho Fire Lookouts' known-staff list places Mike Taylor, its last-named staffer, under the year 1994.
Wikipedia/NRHP account: tower remained in service until 1997, when it was decommissioned; site unstaffed after this year.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register.
A bear damaged the ground cabin's porch logs, posts and decking while foraging for carpenter ants.
Payette National Forest staff, packers and volunteers completed an 11-day, ~100-mile trip to stabilize the cabin.

evidence.supports: 72-foot Aermotor tower, 7,500-ft peak, Payette National Forest, Frank Church Wilderness
evidence.quote: The 72' Aermotor tower with metal 7' x 7' cab atop a 7,516' mountain in Idaho's Payette National Forest
The cabin was added as a residence for the lookouts in 1939.
during WWII, it was used to look for Japanese Balloon Bombs

evidence.supports: Mike Taylor last known named staffer (listed under 1994, not 1997)

evidence.quote: It remained in use for its intended purpose until 1997, when it was decommissioned.
it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994

In 2013, the cabin had also sustained damage from a bear.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states 1935; the NRHP nomination (reflected on Wikipedia) states 1936. Both are kept in the story as a disagreement rather than resolved.

Fact-check (2026-10-04) found the original draft conflated two different sources: Idaho Fire Lookouts' known-staff list places its last-named staffer, Mike Taylor, under the year 1994, not 1997; the 1997 decommissioning date comes from Wikipedia/the NRHP account and does not name a staffer. The story and this file now attribute each fact to its actual source instead of merging them into one 1997/Taylor claim.

notes_for_editor: Build year discrepancy (1935 vs 1936) between NHLR and NRHP/Wikipedia is called out directly in the story rather than silently picking one. Did not verify current structural condition beyond the 2020 Forest Service account; no evidence found of a rental program (site is in designated wilderness and has no road access).
